selected_result: Comparison of inverse row sums for Chebyshev-Vandermonde and Vandermonde matrices

bibliographic_source.title: Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms, 2nd ed., Chapter 22: Vandermonde Systems, Problem 22.5

paper_locations.anchor: Problem 22.5: the inequality between inverse row sums and the resulting infinity-norm comparison

task_clarification: Let T = T(alpha_0,...,alpha_n) = (T_i(alpha_j)) be the Chebyshev-Vandermonde matrix, where T_j is the Chebyshev polynomial of degree j, and write T^{-1} = (u_ij).
Let V = V(alpha_0,...,alpha_n) be the ordinary Vandermonde matrix on the same nodes, with V^{-1} = (w_ij).
Formalize sum_{j=0}^{n} |u_ij| <= sum_{j=0}^{n} |w_ij| for each i.
scope_constraints: Nodes are distinct so that both matrices are nonsingular.
The Chebyshev polynomials are the first-kind polynomials T_j used by the source.
This is an exact matrix-analytic comparison; no rounding model is involved.
Represent both inverses and prove the row-sum inequality rather than assuming it.
